title: Integral closure of an affine torsion-free monoid algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P$ a fine commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], such that $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is torsion free. Put $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{g\in G:ng\in P\text{ for some integer }n>0\}$. For a submonoid $Q\subseteq G$ write $k[Q]=\bigoplus_{q\in Q}ke^q$, with multiplication $e^qe^{q'}=e^{q+q'}$. The natural maps embed $k[P]\subseteq k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]\subseteq k[G]$, all three rings are integral domains, and they have the same fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])$. Inside $K$, $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is the integral closure of $k[P]$: it is exactly the set of elements of $K$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $k[P]$. Moreover $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is a finite $k[P]$-module and is integrally closed in $K$. The zero-rank case $P=G=\{0\}$ and monoids with nontrivial units are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Put $Q=P^{\mathrm{sat}}$. Since $P$ is fine, it is finitely generated and embeds in $G$. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], $Q$ is finitely generated, integral and saturated, its group completion is $G$, and $k[Q]$ is a finite $k[P]$-module. This proves the finiteness clause and supplies the finite-generation hypothesis for $Q$ used next.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-domain-fraction] to $P\subseteq G$ and to $Q\subseteq G$. Both monoids are finitely generated and generate the torsion-free group $G$. The monomial maps embed $k[P]\subseteq k[Q]\subseteq k[G]$, all three are domains, and their fraction fields identify with $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])$. In particular the inclusion is $k[G]\subseteq K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: For each $g\in Q$, the monomial criterion [lem-trf-monomial-integrality] gives that $e^g$ is integral over $k[P]$. The final clause of that node gives that every element of $k[Q]$ is integral over $k[P]$. Thus $k[Q]$ is contained in the integral closure of $k[P]$ inside $K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: The finite generators of $P$ generate $G$ as a group, and $G$ is torsion free by hypothesis. By [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free], choose a finite basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. Put $H=\sum_i\mathbf N u_i$ and $C=k[H]$. By [lem-trf-basis-cone-polynomial-normal], $C$ is a normal domain, identified with the iterated polynomial ring by $X_i\mapsto e^{u_i}$. By [lem-trf-basis-cone-group-localization], $\theta:S^{-1}C\simeq k[G]$ for the basis monomials $S$, with $0\notin S$ and the explicit positive/negative-coordinate inverse. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] to $C,S$: $S^{-1}C$ is a normal domain. The ring isomorphism $\theta$ transports this, so $k[G]$ is a normal domain, i.e. integrally closed in $\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])=K$. Thus every element of $K$ satisfying a monic equation over $k[G]$ lies in $k[G]$, also when $r=0$.

source.place: ILO VIII Lemma 3.2.12 proof, p.104; normal polynomial basis-cone algebra and explicit lattice localization; Stacks Tag 00GY, algebra.tex, lemma-localize-normal-domain.

proof.text: Let $x\in K$ be integral over $k[P]$. A monic equation $x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$ with $a_i\in k[P]$ is also a monic equation over $k[G]$, because $k[P]\subseteq k[G]$. The ambient-field assertion just proved implies $x\in k[G]$. Only now write its finite support $x=\sum_{g\in T}c_ge^g$. By [lem-trf-integral-support-saturation], every $g\in T$ belongs to $Q$. Therefore $x\in k[Q]$. Together with Step 3, this proves that $k[Q]$ is exactly the integral closure of $k[P]$ in $K$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its proof, printed p.104, specialized to S=Spec(k) and F=Spec_mon(P) with torsion-free group completion; finite saturation is 3.1.17 and the finite-map sentence of that proof. No Stacks tag states this monoid-algebra normalization identification.

proof.text: Finally let $y\in K$ be integral over $k[Q]$. Its monic equation also has coefficients in $k[G]$, so Step 4 gives $y\in k[G]$. By Step 1, $Q$ is finitely generated and saturated, with torsion-free group completion $G$. Apply [lem-trf-saturated-monoid-algebra-normal] to $Q$ and this element $y$ of $k[G]$: its statement gives $y\in k[Q]$. This proves integral closedness in the full field $K$, rather than only in the group algebra. All arguments allow $r=0$ and negative basis coordinates, so neither the zero-rank case nor monoids with units require an exception.
